content.intro: This lesson focuses on secrets and sensitive configuration and connects the PDF syllabus topics to a small, inspectable example. Work from the intended data model, write down the expected result, then verify syntax and semantics with the target tool.
content.why_it_matters: Secrets and Sensitive Configuration matters because structured-data files sit between people, tools, services, and deployment systems. A clear contract and repeatable checks make the result easier to maintain and safer to consume.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Untrusted structured data must be bounded, parsed safely, validated for structure and business meaning, and logged without secrets. YAML custom tags and unsafe constructors require particular care, and errors should fail safely.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly addresses: API keys and credentials. Environment variables and secret stores. Secret references in configuration.; Redaction in logs. Excluding secrets from version control. Access control. Rotation and incident response procedures.. Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Secrets and Sensitive Configuration
content_blocks.code:
database:
  host: db.internal.example.invalid
  username: app-user
  password: ${DB_PASSWORD}
# The placeholder is not a real credential; resolve it from a secure secret source at runtime.
content_blocks.expected_output: Keep actual credentials out of source-controlled config. Ensure placeholders are resolved safely and secrets are not echoed into logs or error messages.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save as example.yaml and validate it with the exact parser/linter used by the target application. For Python experiments, use an isolated environment and safe loading for untrusted content. Do not assume every parser resolves ambiguous scalars identically.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the starting fixture before each test. Change one field, indentation level, parser option, or schema constraint at a time, then compare the result with the prediction.
content_blocks.limitations: This snippet is a reference/example, not evidence that the CodeLeaf browser executes JSON/YAML parsing, shell commands, or Python. Validate locally with a named parser or tool before relying on it.
